Smt. Barfi vs Ashok on 24 December, 2025
 Fao-2499-2000(O&M) 1
 In The High Court Of Punjab And Haryana

At Chandigarh
 (201) Fao-2499-2000(O&M)
 Date of Decision-24.12
 Barfi And Others ... Appellants
 Versus
 Ashok And Others ... Respondents
 Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Virinder Aggarwal
 Present: Mr. Ranvijay Singh, Advocate,
 for appellants.

Mr. Manvi Verma, Advocate
 Mr. Rajneesh Malhotra, Advocate
 for respondent No.3-Insurance Company.

*****
 Virinder Aggarwal, J.(Oral)
1.

This appeal has been preferred by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation awarded vide award dated 18.01.2000 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rewari, whereby the compensation of 3,05,000/- along with interest at 12% per annum was granted on account of death of Roshan Lal in a motor vehicular accident that took place on 21.02.1997.
BACKGROUND FACTS 2.
The brief facts of the case are that on 21.02.1997, Roshan Lal, aged about 36 years and Ram niwas, was waiting for some vehicle for going to Pali Railway Station.
In the meantime a bus bearing No. RJ-02-0185 driven by respondent no.1, namely Ashok at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner.
Thereafter, the bus struck against the Roshan lal and as a result of which he received injures and died at the spot.
Thereafter, the claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of 4,00,000/- on account of the death of Roshan Lal.

3. Upon appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence on record, the learned Tribunal concluded that the accident in question and the resultant death of Roshan Lal were duly proved and occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus driven by respondent No.1 Ashok Kumar.

The finding on negligence was primarily founded on the ocular testimony of Ram Niwas (PW- Smt. Barfi vs Ashok on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41380922/
1 2) and Bahadur Singh (PW-3).

Their version was found to be natural, consistent and reliable, and stood corroborated by the registration of FIR (Ex.P1) under Sections 279 and 304-A IPC at Police Station Khol, as well as by the post- mortem report (Ex.P-2), which established that Roshan Lal had succumbed to ante-mortem injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
While assessing the compensation, the learned Tribunal determined the age of the deceased as 34 years.

In the absence of any documentary evidence, the learned Tribunal, adopting a realistic approach keeping in view the nature of his avocation and the prevailing minimum wages for unskilled labour at the relevant time, assessed his monthly income at 2,100.
Thereafter, the learned Tribunal deducted the 1/3rd of his income for his personal expenses and his monthly contribution to the family was assessed at 1,400, i.e. 16,800 per annum.
By applying a multiplier of 17, the loss of dependency was computed at 2,85,600.
Further, the learned Tribunal awarded a sum of 20,000 under conventional heads towards funeral expenses and loss of consortium.
Consequently, the learned Tribunal awarded the total compensation payable to the claimants at 3,05,000/-, together with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
CONTENTIONS 4.

Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the compensation determined by the learned Tribunal is manifestly inadequate and contrary to the settled principles governing the assessment of just compensation.
It was contended that the learned Tribunal erred in assessing the income of the deceased at an unduly low figure, ignoring the evidence on record.
Further, learned counsel argued that the multiplier applied by the learned Tribunal is erroneous and not in consonance with the age of the deceased.

Learned counsel for appellants also submitted that the amounts awarded towards loss of consortium and last rites are unrealistically low and that the learned Tribunal failed to award compensation under other mandatory conventional heads.
Additionally, no addition towards future prospects was made.
On these grounds, it was urged that the impugned award calls for enhancement so as to grant just, fair and reasonable compensation to the claimants.

5. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 supported the award of the learned Tribunal, contended that the award had been passed after a proper and thorough appreciation of the evidence on record and therefore, did not warrant any interference by this Court.
OBSERVATIONS AND FINDINGS 6.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the complete records.
On due consideration of the findings recorded by the learned Tribunal, particularly on the issue of negligence and fastening of liability, I find no reason to take a different view.
The findings on those aspects are accordingly affirmed.
However, the core issue arising in the appeal pertains to the reassessment of the quantum of compensation.

7. Compensation requires reassessment strictly in terms of the principles laid down by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, (2017) 16 SCC 680, Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram, 2018 (18) SCC 130 and Sarla Verma v. DTC,
(2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein the framework for computation of "loss of dependency" by addition towards future prospects as per the nature of employment, deducting personal expenses of deceased, and applying appropriate multiplier on the basis of age of the deceased, and standardized Smt. Barfi vs Ashok on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41380922/
2 amounts for conventional heads such as loss of estate, funeral expenses and loss of consortium, has been settled.

The reassessment is structured as under:
REASSESSED COMPUTATION Particulars Tribunal Award Reassessed Award ()
() Monthly Income 2,100/- 2,100/-
 Income With Future Prospects x 2,940/-
 (40%) (2,100 + 84  Income after Deduction 1,400/- 2,205/-
 (4 Dependents) (1/3rd for personal (1/4th for pe  expenses) expense)
 Annual Contribution To Family 16,800/- 26,460/-
 (1,400 x 12) (2,205 x 1  Loss Of Dependency 2,85,600 4,23,360/-
 (26,460    Spousal Consortium 40,000/-
 Parental Consortium 10,000 80,000/-
 (2 Children) (40,000    Filial Consortium x 40,000/-
 Funeral Expenses 10,000   Loss Of Estate x
Resultantly, the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal is enhanced from 3,05,000/- to 6,13,360/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry the interest at rate of 7% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.
The liability and apportionment of the compensation shall remain the same as determined by the learned Tribunal.
